clue.text: Behaviour, typical of fools (rather than angels), bearskin disguises

definitions.text: Behaviour, typical of fools (rather than angels)
definitions.note: a plural noun naming a kind of behaviour: sudden incursions, as fools rush in where angels fear to tread

indicators.note: to disguise something is to alter its look, so the letters of the fur hat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier's tall fur hat conceals the reckless conduct of fools, as opposed to angels.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'fools rush in where angels fear to tread'.
explanation.definitionFit: Incursions or forcible entries are exactly what the proverb's fools do in rushing ahead.

clue.text: … almost completely ruining airbag clutched by faint-heart as well

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: in toto means completely

indicators.note: held inside the coward's word

parts.note: a hen, or chicken, is a coward

indicators.note: ruining means the letters are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Continuing 27: a ruined airbag clutched by a coward, as well.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TOTO loses its last letter; 'ruining' turns AIRBAG into BARGAI, held in HEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition, besides, as an extra beyond what was expected.

clue.text: Rise in appearance money's in black and white — it's great jazzman's fare

indicators.note: the reversed fee goes inside the two colour letters

parts.note: B is black, as on pencils
W is white

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a fee is money paid for appearing
Duke Ellington was a great jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: A jazz great's fee rises, recorded in black and white, and he eats well.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish of fillet in pastry is food, and fare means food served at a meal.

clue.text: Energy required, perhaps, to thaw this woman?

parts.note: E is energy in physics
to un-ice something, a made-up verb, is to thaw it

explanation.surface: Energy is needed to warm up a cold woman.
explanation.walkthrough: UNICE is an invented word for 'de-ice', hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so it can stand for a particular woman, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Sparkling wine drink to avoid when climbing above Scots town

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first pieces sit above the last

parts.note: kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing reads upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to duck is to avoid
bright means sparkling

explanation.surface: A warning about a sparkling wine cocktail best avoided by climbers in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparkling wine' looks like one phrase; it splits into BRIGHT and the wine drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The town in Galloway, south-west Scotland, gave its name to an old county.

clue.text: "Twisted" Jack going after call girl? It's funny you should say that!

definitions.text: It's funny you should say that!

indicators.note: twisted round, the assembled letters are read backwards
Jack's word goes after the call girl's word

parts.note: tom is British slang for a prostitute
in cribbage the jack of the turned-up suit is 'his nob', so jack can be nob

explanation.surface: A quip about a twisted Jack trailing a call girl, as if a comedian were setting up a punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: TOM is British slang for a prostitute, and the cribbage jack is 'his nob'. The French phrase means a witty remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A witty remark or quip is what a speaker produces when the listener finds their words amusing.

clue.text: I stay positive once eliminated from rough competitions

indicators.note: the letters of the word for 'once' are taken out of the larger word
roughed up, the remaining letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A contestant knocked out of tough competitions insists on staying upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove O, N, C, E from COMPETITIONS and rearrange MPTITIOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hopeful person keeps a cheerful outlook, the speaker's description of themself.

clue.text: Consumer warning seen on toolbox?

definitions.meaning: an allergy notice on food packaging
a label for a box that holds ... and bolts

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a consumer warning label belongs on a toolbox.
explanation.definitionFit: Food labels alert allergy sufferers, and a toolbox literally might hold metal fasteners.

clue.text: Following scrap, obstreperous types viewed here?

definitions.text: Following scrap, obstreperous types viewed here?

parts.words: Following scrap, obstreperous types viewed here?
parts.note: after a fight, unruly children are sent to sit in the parents' punishment spot and be seen

explanation.surface: After a fight, troublemakers are put on show somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents send misbehaving children to sit on a stair as a time-out punishment.

clue.text: Demigod is one who can't stop drinking tea with a little bit of rum in it

definitions.note: the clue gives a noun; the answer is an adjective, divine and human at once, used to describe such a being

indicators.note: the joining word and the letter go inside the tea-drinker, 'it' pointing back to that person

parts.words: one who can't stop drinking tea
parts.note: a theic is someone who drinks tea to excess
and means with, joining two things

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the spirit is taken

explanation.surface: A demigod portrayed as a compulsive tea drinker who laces the cup with a drop of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: THEIC (a tea addict) holds AND plus R, the first letter of 'rum', flagged by 'a little bit of'.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something both divine and human, the defining nature of a half-god figure.

clue.text: Modifying article header removed hard feelings

indicators.note: modifying means changing, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor changes the headline on an article to smooth over ill feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means talked frankly to dispel tension or resentment between people.

clue.text: "Labiate" — how date may be spoken of?

definitions.note: a labiate is a plant of the mint family, such as sage or basil

indicators.note: said aloud, the word for a date sounds like the herb

parts.note: a date is a particular time

explanation.surface: A botanical term set beside a question about how a calendar date is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The herb belongs to the mint family, whose members are called labiates for their lipped flowers.

clue.text: Head for Irish church's best sward to sit with a refreshing drink

indicators.note: only the head, the first letter, of the word is used

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the cream is the best part
sward is turf, a sod

explanation.surface: An Irish church's finest lawn becomes a place to sit with a cool drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A soda topped with a scoop of frozen dessert is a classic cooling beverage.

clue.text: See 1
See 2
Jack's lean (he left a fat-free order)

definitions.note: a jack is a sailor, and a ship's lean to one side is nautical language for it

indicators.note: put in order, the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: free of fat: those three letters are removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Echoes Jack Sprat, who could eat no fat, with a note that he left an order without fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack's lean' recalls Jack Sprat, but Jack is a sailor and lean is a verb-noun for tilting. Removing F, A, T from HELEFTA leaves HELE, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships tilt to one side under wind; sailors call that tilting by this nautical word.

clue.text: Put in residence for men only, one details home

parts.note: to put in is to add
a stag party or night is for men only

explanation.surface: Someone is placed in a men-only residence, with details of their home recorded.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage label giving where the owner lives carries the details of their home.

clue.text: 'ook doesn't have what it takes to succeed thus

definitions.text: 'ook doesn't have what it takes to succeed thus

parts.words: 'ook doesn't have what it takes to succeed thus
parts.note: the dropped H of 'ook fails to be pronounced, and an ambitious person must aspire, hence a pun

explanation.surface: A dropped-H word lacks what it takes to get on in life.
explanation.definitionFit: To breathe an H sound at the start of a word, which 'ook fails to do.

clue.text: Test centre backs American buying and selling safety structure

indicators.note: goes backwards, so the testing place is reversed

parts.note: a lab is a centre for testing
US is American
trade is buying and selling

explanation.surface: A testing centre supports an American firm dealing in safety structures.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing on balusters guards a staircase or balcony, keeping people from falling.

clue.text: Jack's lean and fantastically fit (salt is fat-free)

definitions.note: a jack is a sailor, and a ship's tilting is described in nautical language

indicators.note: done fantastically, the letters are wildly rearranged

parts.note: free of fat: those three letters are removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: Jack is lean and very fit, with the salt free of fat, a healthy diet note.
explanation.walkthrough: As at 15, Jack is a sailor. Taking F, A, T out of FIT plus SALT leaves ISLT, which 'fantastically' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel tilting over to one side is said in sailing terms to do this.

clue.text: Dullard sporting a sleeveless jacket

parts.note: a jerk is a fool, a dullard
sporting means wearing, in

explanation.surface: A dim-witted man shows off his sleeveless jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting short coat without sleeves, traditionally of leather.

clue.text: Impresario's game changing direction for 25's accompaniment?

indicators.note: one compass point, west, is swapped for the opposite one, east

parts.note: an impresario's business is staging and managing shows

explanation.surface: An impresario's line of work takes a new turn, to supply a runner's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: W (west) becomes E (east). 25 is TRACKSUIT, the warm-up gear the footwear goes with.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic trainers are the natural footwear worn with a warm-up outfit.

clue.text: See 7
See 8
Organ transplants within body cavities

indicators.note: the letters sit within the run of the two words

explanation.surface: Organ transplants placed inside the body's cavities, as in surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the plural of antrum names hollow chambers such as the sinuses.

clue.text: Retiring Welsh runner pursuing clubs in characteristic warm-up gear

indicators.note: the clubs and river go inside the word for a characteristic

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic

indicators.note: the river comes after the clubs

parts.note: C is clubs in cards

indicators.note: going back, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Usk is a river in Wales; a river runs

explanation.surface: A retiring Welsh athlete trails behind the clubs in warm-up gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh runner' looks like an athlete; it is the Usk, a Welsh river, turned to KSU by 'Retiring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose two-piece outfit is worn by athletes for warming up before an event.

clue.text: Stake fixed by partners in French city

indicators.note: held in place by the partners on either side

parts.note: N and S, North and South, are partners in bridge
an ante is a stake in poker

explanation.surface: A stake agreed between partners in some French city deal.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Loire is a major port and regional capital in western France.

clue.text: After time, gets down ski run, crashing into old pro's midriff …

indicators.note: the jumbled letters break into the middle pair
the midriff is the middle, so the central letters of the phrase are taken
crashing means the letters of the two words are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A skier tumbles down a run and crashes into a former professional's stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets down' suggests descending the slope, but it means swallowing; the ellipsis hands the clue on to 1 Down. The midriff spans both words of 'old pro'.
explanation.definitionFit: When the barman calls time, patrons finish their glasses, swallowing the last of their beer.
